$comment: Advisories the npm audit gate will not fail on, each scoped to ONE advisory in ONE directory.
This is not a suppression list. A suppression says 'ignore this'; every entry here is a claim
with a stated premise and an expiry date, and the gate FAILS when either stops holding:
expires       the entry is dead after this date. An expired entry is RED, never skipped --
so a finding parked here resurfaces on its own instead of being parked forever.
absent_globs  files whose ABSENCE the exception depends on. If any of these paths comes to
exist, the premise is broken and the entry stops covering anything.
An advisory that is not listed here is RED. An entry that no longer matches anything is also RED,
because a stale exception is one nobody is reading, and the correct response to a fixed advisory
is to delete its entry rather than leave it lying where the next reader will trust it.
Adding an entry is a security decision. Justify reachability from evidence, not from intuition.
